args.rationale: 69-year-old man with advanced lung adenocarcinoma, on pembrolizumab (first dose 14 days ago), with deep jaundice, dark stools, lethargy and lightheadedness. Hemoglobin is 45 g/L, down from a baseline of 123 g/L. He is currently hemodynamically preserved (HR 92, SBP 115), but the acute drop is large and he is symptomatic. Cause is uncertain: immune-related hemolytic anemia, upper GI bleed, immune hepatitis/cholangitis, or malignant biliary obstruction. He needs close monitoring, transfusion, and urgent workup.
args.followup_or_handoff: Handoff to ICU/GI/oncology. Continue transfusion of crossmatched PRBCs with repeat Hb after each unit. Continue IV pantoprazole. Urgent EGD. Obtain the labs not reported so far: bilirubin fractionation, LFTs, platelets, creatinine, INR, LDH, haptoglobin, reticulocytes, smear and DAT. Get hepatobiliary imaging (US or CT/MRCP). Hold pembrolizumab. If hemolysis or immune-related hepatitis is confirmed, start high-dose corticosteroids (e.g., prednisone/methylprednisolone 1-2 mg/kg/day) with oncology/hematology input. Reassess the diagnosis with the new results.
